title: An Easter Basket Display
description: Look over an Easter basket through familiar container parts, soft linings, and decorative details.
cardDescription: Look over an Easter basket through familiar container parts, soft linings, and decorative details.
focus: The clues describe the basket and things placed around it. A material, a shape, and a finished object have different names.
solvingTip: Look for the container, one of its parts, or a small added decoration.
words: Woven container used for a familiar Easter display
Curved part used to carry a basket
To interlace strips into a basket structure
Decorative fabric strip tied to an Easter basket
Looped knot made from a decorative strip
Material placed against the inside of a basket
Plantlike strands used in a seasonal basket display
Thin sheet material used for basket decorations
Soft thin wrapping placed around a gift
Oval symbol commonly placed in an Easter display
Sweet confection tucked into a holiday basket
Small attached label identifying a basket’s recipient
Written greeting placed with a seasonal gift

answerNotes.LINER: A liner covers an inside surface. It differs from the basket’s outer woven structure.
answerNotes.WEAVE: Weave is a construction action. The clue asks for interlacing rather than one individual strip.
answerNotes.TISSUE: Tissue means soft paper here. It is not the biological material with the same spelling.
answerNotes.BOW: Bow is the looped knot and rhymes with go. Ribbon names the material from which it can be made.

title: Patterns on an Easter Egg
description: Explore egg parts and decorative patterns through familiar colors, marks, and small tools.
cardDescription: Explore egg parts and decorative patterns through familiar colors, marks, and small tools.
focus: The clues identify physical parts and visible designs. The words describe the objects rather than giving a dyeing procedure.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for an egg part, a color material, or a pattern.
words: Oval object with a shell used in a familiar spring decoration
Hard outside covering of an egg
Yellow or orange central part of an egg
Clear part of a raw egg surrounding the yolk
Coloring material used to tint an egg’s surface
Visible hue on a decorated shell
Bristled tool used to add a painted pattern
Material used to resist dye in some egg-decorating traditions
Repeated or arranged design on a decorated object
Small separate area of contrasting color
Tiny round mark in a decorative pattern
Flat support used to hold several decorated eggs

answerNotes.DYE: Dye colors a material. It sounds like die, the singular game cube, but has a different spelling.
answerNotes.YOLK: The yolk is the central egg portion. Its color can range from yellow to orange.
answerNotes.WHITE: White names the egg portion around the yolk. It is a noun here rather than just a color description.
answerNotes.WAX: Wax can resist dye in decorative techniques. The clue identifies its role without giving a recipe or method.

title: A Spring Sunday Lunch
description: Gather familiar meal words for a spring holiday table and its simple serving objects.
cardDescription: Gather familiar meal words for a spring holiday table and its simple serving objects.
focus: The clues name foods, tableware, and a visitor’s role. Direct descriptions keep the focus on everyday vocabulary.
solvingTip: Look for a food, a serving object, or a person sharing the meal.
words: Meal eaten around the middle of the day
Cured pork traditionally served at many spring holiday meals
Large piece of food cooked with dry heat
Individual bread served with a meal
Small round green seeds commonly served as a vegetable
Root vegetable often pictured as orange and tapered
Dish combining raw vegetables or other prepared ingredients
Flat dish holding one guest’s meal
Pronged utensil used at the lunch table
Cloth or paper square provided to a diner
Person invited to share a spring meal

answerNotes.HAM: Ham is a cured pork food in this clue. It can also describe an exaggerated performer in informal language.
answerNotes.ROAST: Roast is a noun for a cooked piece of food here. The same word can be the cooking action.
answerNotes.ROLL: A roll is an individual bread in this setting. It is not a movement or a list of names.
answerNotes.GUEST: Guest identifies an invited person’s role. It does not name a family relationship.

title: An Easter Bonnet
description: Explore a traditional spring outfit through familiar hat parts, clothing, and decorative details.
cardDescription: Explore a traditional spring outfit through familiar hat parts, clothing, and decorative details.
focus: The clues identify objects by where they are worn or located. Some answers name whole garments, while others name an edge or a fastening.
solvingTip: Use head, wrist, neck, and lower-edge locations to distinguish the clothing words.
words: Hat style associated with a traditional Easter outfit
Head covering decorated for a spring parade
Fabric strip arranged around a festive hat
Projecting edge around the lower part of a hat
Upper main part of a hat
Strip encircling the base of a hat’s crown
Hand covering worn with a dress outfit
Long fabric accessory worn around the neck
Outer garment worn over an outfit
Small fastener sewn to a spring coat
Part of a garment surrounding the neck
Folded finished edge at the bottom of clothing
Foot covering worn as part of an outfit

answerNotes.BRIM: The brim projects outward from a hat. The crown is the main upper part above it.
answerNotes.CROWN: Crown means a hat part here. It is not a royal ornament in this clothing clue.
answerNotes.HEM: A hem is an edge finish. Its lower position distinguishes it from the collar at the neck.
answerNotes.BONNET: Bonnet names a hat in this clue. The seasonal context points to headwear rather than other regional meanings.

title: At the Easter Baking Counter
description: Browse familiar bread, dried-fruit, and sweet-coating words around a spring bakery display.
cardDescription: Browse familiar bread, dried-fruit, and sweet-coating words around a spring bakery display.
focus: The clues describe baked goods and their ingredients or shapes. They provide word meanings rather than a complete recipe.
solvingTip: Look for a bread form, a flavoring, a finishing material, or a surface feature.
words: Small bread associated with a cross-topped Easter treat
Shape marked on top of a familiar spiced holiday bun
Unbaked flour mixture that can be shaped into bread
Organism used to make many bread doughs expand
Dried grape used in some spiced buns
Small dried grape used in traditional baking
Thin coating adding a smooth finish to a bun
Whole shaped bread before it is sliced
Interwoven shape used for some festive breads
Milled grain powder used to make bread dough
Aromatic flavoring added to a festive bun
Flat baking or serving support for small breads
Baked outer surface of a bread
Sweet mixture used to draw a pattern on baked goods

answerNotes.BRAID: Braid names an interwoven shape. The clue uses it for bread rather than hair.
answerNotes.GLAZE: A glaze is a thin surface coating. It differs from the dough inside the bread.
answerNotes.CURRANT: A baking currant can be a small dried grape. The clue uses that meaning rather than a fresh red or black currant.
answerNotes.CROSS: Cross names the marked shape here. It is not an instruction to move from one side to another.
